olmecs.name: Olmecs
olmecs.summary: An early Mesoamerican civilization that flourished roughly 1200 to 400 BC in what is now Veracruz and Tabasco, known for colossal stone heads and considered one of the cradles of civilization.

nixtamalization.name: Nixtamalization
nixtamalization.summary: A process of soaking and cooking maize in an alkaline solution such as limewater, which improves its nutrition and flavor and makes it possible to form dough (masa).

felipe-calder-n.name: Felipe Calderón
felipe-calder-n.summary: President of Mexico from 2006 to 2012, previously Secretary of Energy under Vicente Fox; his presidency was marked by declaring war on the country's drug cartels ten days after taking office.

diana-kennedy.name: Diana Kennedy
diana-kennedy.summary: A British food writer (1923–2022) regarded as the leading English-language authority on Mexican cuisine, known for books drawn from fifty years of travel and research across Mexico.

the-cuisines-of-mexico.name: The Cuisines of Mexico
the-cuisines-of-mexico.summary: Diana Kennedy's first of nine cookbooks, credited with introducing Americans to Mexican food beyond Tex-Mex.

robb-walsh.name: Robb Walsh
robb-walsh.summary: American food writer and former Houston Press restaurant critic (2000-2010), author of more than a dozen food books including The Tex-Mex Cookbook and Texas Eats, and a three-time James Beard Award winner.

bracero-program.name: Bracero Program
bracero-program.summary: A 1942–1964 US–Mexico labor program allowing Mexican workers into US agriculture and railroads; studies later found it did not hurt American-born workers' wages.

felix-tijerina.name: Felix Tijerina
felix-tijerina.summary: Mexican-American restaurateur, activist and philanthropist in Houston (1905–1965) who served as national president of LULAC.

league-of-united-latin-american-citizens.name: LULAC
league-of-united-latin-american-citizens.summary: The largest and oldest Hispanic civil rights organization in the United States, founded in 1929 in Corpus Christi, Texas, largely by Hispanic World War I veterans.
league-of-united-latin-american-citizens.source_title: League of United Latin American Citizens

daniela-soto-innes.name: Daniela Soto-Innes
daniela-soto-innes.summary: Mexican-born chef, the youngest ever named World's Best Female Chef, who helped open Cosme in New York in 2014 and later opened Atla.

diego-rivera.name: Diego Rivera
diego-rivera.summary: Mexican painter, 1886 to 1957, whose large frescoes helped establish the Mexican mural movement; he painted murals across Mexico and the United States, including a 27-piece series in Detroit.

jos-clemente-orozco.name: José Clemente Orozco
jos-clemente-orozco.summary: Mexican painter (1883–1949) who, with Diego Rivera and David Alfaro Siqueiros, founded the Mexican Mural Renaissance, painting political murals influenced by Symbolism.

david-alfaro-siqueiros.name: David Alfaro Siqueiros
david-alfaro-siqueiros.summary: A Mexican social realist painter (1896–1974) known for large public murals, one of the most famous Mexican muralists alongside Diego Rivera and José Clemente Orozco.

chicano-art-movement.name: Chicano art movement
chicano-art-movement.summary: A movement by Mexican-American artists, beginning in the 1960s, to build a distinct cultural identity drawing on pre-Columbian art and civil-rights era politics.

luis-barrag-n.name: Luis Barragán
luis-barrag-n.summary: Mexican architect and engineer (1902–1988) whose influential work won him the 1980 Pritzker Prize, architecture's highest honor.

am-rica-tropical-oprimida-y-destrozada-p.name: América Tropical
am-rica-tropical-oprimida-y-destrozada-p.summary: A 1932 fresco mural by David Alfaro Siqueiros in Los Angeles that was painted over soon after completion and restored and reopened to the public in 2012.
am-rica-tropical-oprimida-y-destrozada-p.source_title: América Tropical: Oprimida y Destrozada por los Imperialismos

getty-conservation-institute.name: Getty Conservation Institute
getty-conservation-institute.summary: Los Angeles-based research institute, part of the J. Paul Getty Trust, dedicated to advancing art and architectural conservation worldwide since 1985.

pomona-college.name: Pomona College
pomona-college.summary: A private liberal arts college in Claremont, California, founded in 1887, known today for its large endowment, selectivity and a student body of roughly 1,700.

jos-ch-vez-morado.name: José Chávez Morado
jos-ch-vez-morado.summary: Mexican muralist (1909–2002) of the generation following Diego Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros, known for major murals in Mexico City and Guanajuato.

estadio-ol-mpico-universitario.name: Estadio Olímpico Universitario
estadio-ol-mpico-universitario.summary: A stadium in Mexico City opened in 1952, once the nation's largest, that served as the main venue for the 1968 Summer Olympics.

mario-pani.name: Mario Pani
mario-pani.summary: Mexican architect and urbanist who shaped much of Mexico City's urban landscape during the Mexican Miracle, designing landmarks such as the UNAM campus and major housing projects.

reed-insurgent-mexico.name: Reed: Insurgent Mexico
reed-insurgent-mexico.summary: A 1973 Mexican drama film by Paul Leduc based on John Reed's book of the same name about the Mexican Revolution, submitted for the Best Foreign Language Film Oscar.

frida-kahlo.name: Frida Kahlo
frida-kahlo.summary: A Mexican painter (1907–1954) known for portraits and self-portraits exploring Mexican identity, whose 1940 self-portrait holds the auction record for a work by a female artist, at $54.7 million.

caste-war-of-yucat-n.name: Caste War of Yucatán
caste-war-of-yucat-n.summary: An 1847–1915 revolt of Indigenous Maya people in Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula against Hispanic control, considered one of the most successful modern Native American uprisings.

zapatista-army-of-national-liberation.name: Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN)
zapatista-army-of-national-liberation.summary: A far-left political and militant organization controlling territory in Chiapas, Mexico, at war with the Mexican state since a 1994 uprising, made up mainly of rural Indigenous people.

lacandon-jungle.name: Lacandon Jungle
lacandon-jungle.summary: A rainforest stretching from Chiapas, Mexico, into Guatemala, home to Maya sites such as Palenque and to the indigenous Lacandon Maya people.

salvador-alvarado.name: Salvador Alvarado
salvador-alvarado.summary: A Mexican general and politician (1880-1924) who served in the Constitutional Army during the Mexican Revolution and was Governor of Yucatán from 1915 to 1918.

porfirio-d-az.name: Porfirio Díaz
porfirio-d-az.summary: Mexican army general and politician who ruled as dictator from 1876 to 1911, serving over thirty years as president, the longest of any Mexican ruler.

nicol-s-guill-n.name: Nicolás Guillén
nicol-s-guill-n.summary: Cuban poet and journalist (1902–1989) regarded as Cuba's national poet, known for blending son music into politically engaged poetry.

dulce-mar-a-loynaz.name: Dulce María Loynaz
dulce-mar-a-loynaz.summary: Cuban poet (1902–1997) considered one of the principal figures of Cuban literature, awarded the Miguel de Cervantes Prize in 1992.

jos-lezama-lima.name: José Lezama Lima
jos-lezama-lima.summary: Cuban writer, poet, and essayist (1910–1976), a leading figure in Latin American literature and Neo-Baroque style, best known for his novel Paradiso.

alejo-carpentier.name: Alejo Carpentier
alejo-carpentier.summary: Cuban novelist, essayist and musicologist (1904–1980) who influenced Latin American literature's "boom" period and pioneered magical realism.

reinaldo-arenas.name: Reinaldo Arenas
reinaldo-arenas.summary: A Cuban poet, novelist and playwright (1943–1990) known as a vocal critic of Fidel Castro; his memoir was published after his 1980 escape to the US.

guillermo-cabrera-infante.name: Guillermo Cabrera Infante
guillermo-cabrera-infante.summary: A Cuban novelist, essayist and critic (1929–2005) who went into exile in London in 1965; best known for the novel Three Trapped Tigers.

da-na-chaviano.name: Daína Chaviano
da-na-chaviano.summary: Cuban-American writer, born 1957 in Havana, considered one of the leading female fantasy and science fiction authors writing in Spanish.

zo-vald-s.name: Zoé Valdés
zo-vald-s.summary: Cuban novelist, poet and film director born in Havana in 1959, who worked for Cuba's UNESCO delegation in Paris in the 1980s and later edited the magazine Cine Cubano.

eliseo-alberto.name: Eliseo Alberto
eliseo-alberto.summary: Cuban-born Mexican writer, novelist and journalist, known for the novel Caracol Beach, who lived from 1951 to 2011.

abilio-est-vez.name: Abilio Estévez
abilio-est-vez.summary: Cuban novelist, playwright and poet born in Havana in 1954, who now lives in Barcelona.

pedro-juan-guti-rrez.name: Pedro Juan Gutiérrez
pedro-juan-guti-rrez.summary: Cuban novelist born in 1950, author of Dirty Havana Trilogy and other works, known for depicting life in Havana's rundown Centro Habana district.

nahuatl.name: Nahuatl
nahuatl.summary: A language of the Uto-Aztecan family spoken in central Mexico since at least the 7th century CE, once the prestige language of the Aztec Empire.

hispanicization.name: Hispanicization
hispanicization.summary: The process by which a place or person becomes influenced by Hispanic culture, or non-Hispanic things become Hispanic, seen in language, food, music and festivals; in former Spanish colonies it can mean Spanish replacing indigenous languages.

ngel-arango.name: Ángel Arango
ngel-arango.summary: Cuban science fiction writer (1926-2013), a pioneer considered the genre's leading exponent on the island.

onelio-jorge-cardoso.name: Onelio Jorge Cardoso
onelio-jorge-cardoso.summary: Cuban editor, screenwriter, short-fiction writer and party functionary (1914–1986) who continued publishing in Cuba during the restrictive 'Quinquenio Gris.'

norberto-fuentes.name: Norberto Fuentes
norberto-fuentes.summary: A Cuban writer and journalist born in 1943, author of the prize-winning Condenados de Condado (1968), and a former close friend of Fidel Castro with inside knowledge of Cuba's secret service.

eduardo-heras-le-n.name: Eduardo Heras León
eduardo-heras-le-n.summary: A Cuban writer and professor (1940-2023) awarded Cuba's National Literature Prize in 2014.

senel-paz.name: Senel Paz
senel-paz.summary: A Cuban author and screenwriter born in 1950, best known for his short story 'The Wolf, the Forest and the New Man,' which he adapted into the film Strawberry and Chocolate (1994).

abel-prieto.name: Abel Prieto
abel-prieto.summary: Cuban politician born in 1950 who served as Minister of Culture from 1997 to 2012 and again from 2016, and advised President Raúl Castro; also a published fiction author.

instituto-polit-cnico-nacional.name: National Polytechnic Institute
instituto-polit-cnico-nacional.summary: One of Mexico's largest public universities, founded on 1 January 1936 during the presidency of Lázaro Cárdenas, based mainly in Mexico City.

monterrey-institute-of-technology-and-hi.name: Monterrey Institute of Technology
monterrey-institute-of-technology-and-hi.summary: A private Mexican research university founded in 1943 by industrialist Eugenio Garza Sada, later the first university outside the US to connect to the internet in the Western Hemisphere.
monterrey-institute-of-technology-and-hi.source_title: Monterrey Institute of Technology and Higher Education

national-autonomous-university-of-mexico.name: UNAM
national-autonomous-university-of-mexico.summary: Mexico's leading public research university, founded in its modern form in 1910; its Mexico City campus is a UNESCO World Heritage site that hosted the 1968 Olympics.

ricardo-miledi.name: Ricardo Miledi
ricardo-miledi.summary: Mexican neuroscientist (1927–2017) known for uncovering the role of calcium in neurotransmitter release and for developing a technique to study receptors in frog egg cells for drug research.

william-t-sanders.name: William T. Sanders
william-t-sanders.summary: American anthropologist (1926–2008) who specialized in the archaeology of Mesoamerica.

teotihuacan.name: Teotihuacan
teotihuacan.summary: An ancient Mesoamerican city near modern Mexico City, home to the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, likely the largest city in the Americas around 1 to 500 CE with up to 100,000 people.

kaminaljuyu.name: Kaminaljuyu
kaminaljuyu.summary: A Pre-Columbian Maya site now within Guatemala City, occupied from about 1500 BCE to 1200 CE and once among the greatest sites in the New World.

cinvestav.name: CINVESTAV
cinvestav.summary: A Mexican scientific research institution founded in 1961 and affiliated with the National Polytechnic Institute, offering graduate studies in fields such as physics, biology and mathematics.

cop-n.name: Copán
cop-n.summary: An archaeological site of the Maya civilization in western Honduras, capital of a major kingdom from the 5th to 9th centuries AD until its abandonment in the early 10th century.

national-academy-of-sciences.name: National Academy of Sciences
national-academy-of-sciences.summary: An American scientific organization established by an Act of Congress in 1863, whose elected members serve as advisers to the nation on science and technology.

lvaro-obreg-n.name: Álvaro Obregón
lvaro-obreg-n.summary: Mexican general and politician who served as the 46th President of Mexico from 1920 to 1924; re-elected in 1928, he was assassinated before taking office.

plutarco-el-as-calles.name: Plutarco Elías Calles
plutarco-el-as-calles.summary: Mexican politician and military officer who served as president of Mexico from 1924 to 1928, then held de facto power as the country's leader during the Maximato from 1929 to 1934.

l-zaro-c-rdenas.name: Lázaro Cárdenas
l-zaro-c-rdenas.summary: Mexican general and revolutionary who served as president from 1934 to 1940, known for land reform, nationalising the oil industry and building a welfare state.

manuel-vila-camacho.name: Manuel Ávila Camacho
manuel-vila-camacho.summary: Mexican politician and military leader who served as president of Mexico from 1940 to 1946, affectionately called "The Gentleman President."

danish-west-indies.name: Danish West Indies
danish-west-indies.summary: A Danish Caribbean colony of Saint Thomas, Saint John and Saint Croix, purchased by the United States in 1917 to become the US Virgin Islands.

institutional-revolutionary-party.name: Institutional Revolutionary Party
institutional-revolutionary-party.summary: Mexican political party founded in 1929 (under an earlier name) that held uninterrupted power in Mexico for 71 years, from 1929 to 2000.

lend-lease.name: Lend-Lease
lend-lease.summary: A US policy of 1941 to 1945 supplying the United Kingdom, Soviet Union, France, China and other Allies with food, oil and materiel worth $50.1 billion, given free as essential to US defense.

ss-potrero-del-llano.name: SS Potrero del Llano
ss-potrero-del-llano.summary: A Mexican-flagged oil tanker torpedoed by a German U-boat off Florida in 1942, an attack that helped push Mexico toward joining the Allies.

german-submarine-u-564.name: U-564
german-submarine-u-564.summary: A Type VIIC German U-boat of World War II, sunk by the RAF in the Bay of Biscay on 14 June 1943.

ss-faja-de-oro.name: SS Faja de Oro
ss-faja-de-oro.summary: A Mexican-flagged oil tanker, originally built in 1914, torpedoed by a German submarine in the Gulf of Mexico in 1942, an event that helped push Mexico toward the Allied side.

german-submarine-u-160.name: U-160
german-submarine-u-160.summary: A Type IXC German U-boat of World War II that served until it was sunk on 14 July 1943.

palo-religion.name: Palo
palo-religion.summary: An African diasporic religion developed in Cuba in the late 19th or early 20th century, drawing on Kongo religious tradition alongside Catholic and Spiritist influences, centered on spirits of the dead.

enrique-dussel.name: Enrique Dussel
enrique-dussel.summary: An Argentine-Mexican academic, philosopher, historian and theologian who served as interim rector of the Universidad Autónoma de la Ciudad de México from 2013 to 2014; he lived 1934–2023.

alfredo-l-pez-austin.name: Alfredo López Austin
alfredo-l-pez-austin.summary: Mexican historian, 1936 to 2021, who wrote extensively on the Aztec worldview and Mesoamerican religion during a roughly fifty-year academic career at UNAM.

nganga.name: Nganga
nganga.summary: A spiritual healer, diviner and ritual specialist in traditional Kongo religion, also found among descendants of Kongo and Mbundu peoples across the African diaspora, including Brazil, Cuba and Haiti.

dependency-theory.name: dependency theory
dependency-theory.summary: The idea that resources flow from poor "periphery" states to wealthy "core" ones, developed after World War II to explain underdevelopment in Latin America.

emmanuel-levinas.name: Emmanuel Levinas
emmanuel-levinas.summary: French philosopher of Lithuanian Jewish ancestry (1906–1995) known for his work in Jewish philosophy, existentialism and phenomenology, focused on the relation of ethics to metaphysics.

paul-gauthier-theologian.name: Paul Gauthier
paul-gauthier-theologian.summary: French Catholic priest and theologian (1914–2002) best known for his contributions to liberation theology.

liberation-theology.name: Liberation theology
liberation-theology.summary: A Christian theological approach that began among Latin American Catholic theologians in the 1960s, stressing liberation of the oppressed through social and economic analysis.

leonardo-l-pez-luj-n.name: Leonardo López Luján
leonardo-l-pez-luj-n.summary: A Mexican archaeologist (born 1964), a leading researcher of pre-Hispanic Central Mexican societies, director of the Templo Mayor Project since 1991, and son of historian Alfredo López Austin.

templo-mayor.name: Templo Mayor
templo-mayor.summary: The main temple of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, dedicated to the war god Huitzilopochtli and rain god Tlaloc, built from around 1325 and destroyed by the Spanish in 1521.

feathered-serpent.name: Feathered Serpent
feathered-serpent.summary: A supernatural deity found across Mesoamerican religions, known as Quetzalcōātl to the Aztecs and Kukulkan to the Maya, its feathers and serpent body symbolizing divine and earthly natures.

c-l-r-james.name: C. L. R. James
c-l-r-james.summary: Trinidadian historian and Marxist writer (1901–1989) best known for The Black Jacobins (1938), a history of the Haitian Revolution, and for influencing postcolonial thought.

the-black-jacobins.name: The Black Jacobins
the-black-jacobins.summary: A 1938 history by Trinidadian historian C. L. R. James of the Haitian Revolution of 1791–1804, centred on the leadership of Toussaint L'Ouverture.

jean-paul-sartre.name: Jean-Paul Sartre
jean-paul-sartre.summary: A French philosopher and writer (1905–1980) and leading figure of existentialism, awarded the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature, which he attempted to refuse.

frantz-fanon.name: Frantz Fanon
frantz-fanon.summary: French psychiatrist and political philosopher (1925–1961) who supported Algerian independence and became one of the most influential anticolonial thinkers of his time.

black-skin-white-masks.name: Black Skin, White Masks
black-skin-white-masks.summary: A 1952 book by philosopher-psychiatrist Frantz Fanon examining the psychological effects of racism and colonial domination.

ngola-title.name: Ngola
ngola-title.summary: The title of the king of the Kingdom of Ndongo, in what is now north-west Angola, from the 16th to 17th century; the country of Angola is named after it.

kingdom-of-kongo.name: Kingdom of Kongo
kingdom-of-kongo.summary: A Central African kingdom spanning parts of modern Angola, Congo and Gabon, independent from around 1390 to 1862, later a Portuguese vassal until its monarchy was abolished in 1914.

yoruba-people.name: Yoruba people
yoruba-people.summary: A West African ethnic group of over 50 million people, mainly in Nigeria, Benin and Togo, and one of Africa's largest ethnic groups.

golden-age-of-mexican-cinema.name: Golden Age of Mexican Cinema
golden-age-of-mexican-cinema.summary: Boom period in Mexican film, 1936 to 1956, when a new generation of directors and actors became lasting icons after wartime decline in US and European filmmaking.

cantinflas.name: Cantinflas
cantinflas.summary: Stage name of Mario Moreno (1911-1993), a Mexican comedian and actor widely known across Latin America and Spain, called the 'Charlie Chaplin of Mexico' and a co-star in Around the World in 80 Days.

pedro-infante.name: Pedro Infante
pedro-infante.summary: Mexican singer and actor (1917–1957) of Mexican cinema's golden age, who appeared in over 60 films and recorded more than 350 songs before dying in a plane crash.

dolores-del-r-o.name: Dolores del Río
dolores-del-r-o.summary: Mexican actress (1904 to 1983) whose 50-year career spanned Hollywood's Golden Age and Mexican cinema's Golden Age; considered the first major Latin American crossover Hollywood star.

mar-a-f-lix.name: María Félix
mar-a-f-lix.summary: Mexican actress and singer (1914–2002), one of the most successful and celebrated figures of the Golden Age of Mexican cinema, known as 'La Doña'.

kongo-religion.name: Kongo religion
kongo-religion.summary: The traditional animistic beliefs of the Bakongo people, centered on the creator god Nzambi Ampungu and on ancestor veneration.

charrer-a.name: Charrería
charrer-a.summary: Mexico's national sport, evolved from cattle-herding and equestrian traditions on colonial haciendas; UNESCO listed it as intangible cultural heritage in 2016.

azteca-horse.name: Azteca horse
azteca-horse.summary: A horse breed developed in Mexico in 1972 from Andalusian, American Quarter Horse and Mexican Criollo bloodlines, used in western and English riding disciplines.

plaza-de-toros-m-xico.name: Plaza México
plaza-de-toros-m-xico.summary: The world's largest bullring, a 41,262-seat venue in Mexico City that opened in 1946, also used for boxing matches.

constitution-of-mexico.name: Constitution of 1917
constitution-of-mexico.summary: Mexico's constitution, drafted during the Mexican Revolution and adopted in 1917, the first in the world to enshrine social rights and one that restricted the Catholic Church's power.

jos-bedia-vald-s.name: José Bedia Valdés
jos-bedia-vald-s.summary: Cuban painter, born in 1959, now living in Florida.

leonardo-padura-fuentes.name: Leonardo Padura Fuentes
leonardo-padura-fuentes.summary: A Cuban novelist and journalist (born 1955) best known for his Mario Conde detective novels and El hombre que amaba a los perros (2009); winner of Cuba's National Prize for Literature in 2012.

tenochtitlan.name: Tenochtitlan
tenochtitlan.summary: The Aztec capital built on an island in Lake Texcoco, founded around 1325, that grew into the largest city in the pre-Columbian Americas before its capture in 1521.

coyolx-uhqui.name: Coyolxāuhqui
coyolx-uhqui.summary: In Aztec religion, a daughter of the goddess Cōātlīcue who led her brothers in an attack on their mother but was defeated by Huītzilōpōchtli; a huge 1978 discovery of her stone relief led to major excavations of the Aztec Templo Mayor.

sylvanus-morley.name: Sylvanus Morley
sylvanus-morley.summary: An American archaeologist, 1883 to 1948, who led excavations of the Maya site of Chichen Itza and wrote influential works on Maya hieroglyphic writing.

j-eric-s-thompson.name: J. Eric S. Thompson
j-eric-s-thompson.summary: An English Mesoamerican archaeologist, ethnohistorian and epigrapher (1898–1975) who dominated Maya studies, especially the study of the Maya script, into the 1960s.

bonampak.name: Bonampak
bonampak.summary: An ancient Maya site in Chiapas, Mexico, built between about 580 and 800 AD and famous for well-preserved murals depicting a battle, first seen by outsiders in 1946.

mesoamerica_caribbean-modern-science-005: Center for Research and Advanced Studies of the National Polytechnic Institute
